A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Logos dataset and cross-language sign recognition study. Their text, tables, equations, and figures are readable and support comparison, including the new Appendices A and B in v2. V1 has no appendix.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.5 and Tables 2–8 report original recognition, transfer-learning, few-shot, label-mapping, and VSSign-grouping experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports transfer-learning and co-training results using MM-WLAuslan as a source dataset.

M1.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 retain the MViTv2-S encoder, classification and boundary-regression losses, language-specific heads, and language-gated CutMix/Mixup. The expanded annotation, splitting, and training descriptions document existing procedures rather than establish a changed method.

E1.justification: MM-WLAuslan, previously only surveyed, becomes an actual Australian Sign Language pre-training and co-training source. AUTSL and WLASL remain the target benchmarks with the same full-data and few-shot tasks. The added K-RSL survey entry does not represent an evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds Uni-Sign and an MM-WLAuslan-based co-training comparator; Table 6 adds MM-WLAuslan pre-training. Existing comparators remain. V2's 'ZBEST' matches v1's BEST through its citation and unchanged 54.6 score, so it is not another comparator.

E3.justification: Section 5.5 changes the reported ungrouped-label ablation from 2,880 to 2,863 classes. This revises a stated experimental configuration without establishing that experiments were rerun. Existing input dimensions, accuracy metric, split proportions, and few-shot designs remain; Appendix B's training settings are newly disclosed rather than demonstrably changed.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 extends the pre-training-source analysis beyond the smaller AUTSL and WLASL datasets to another large corpus, MM-WLAuslan, testing source choice in both transfer learning and co-training. The label-mapping generalization check and VSSign-grouping analyses otherwise retain their evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional comparisons retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes full-data AUTSL accuracy from 95.25 to 97.25; Table 2 changes Logos accuracy under Logos+WLASL co-training from 97.92 to 97.93. New results include MM-WLAuslan co-training accuracies of 97.43/64.59, its four transfer scores in Table 6, and Uni-Sign's 63.5 WLASL score. The headline Logos-based 97.81/66.82 results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 and Algorithm 1 newly formalize the split criterion using per-gloss sample proportions, maximum deviation from the target ratio, and swap-update equations. V1 only describes an approximate balanced split. This is a limited addition of formal specification; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: V2 removes the introduction's categorical assertion that no previous research investigates large-dataset cross-language encoders and acknowledges multilingual-dataset training. This narrows novelty positioning. The principal claims about Logos, VSSign grouping, multi-head co-training, and WLASL performance remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds linguistic justification for combining polysemy and minimal pairs as VSSigns, explains the practical focus on frontal RGB input, and frames AUTSL/WLASL as models of low-resource settings. The limitations replace the explicit racial-bias warning with RSL-specific applicability concerns, while retaining age/gender and architecture limitations.

D1.justification: V2 supplies substantial previously missing reproducibility information: five-expert majority annotation, proficiency testing, collection and validation rules, annotation aggregation, split pseudocode, detailed sampling and augmentations, and hardware, optimizer, learning-rate, and training-duration specifications. Appendices A–B distinguish these disclosures from procedural innovations. The main code, dataset, and model access statement remains.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion or citations for SignCLIP, Uni-Sign, K-RSL, Ebling et al. (2015), and Mukushev et al. (2020), while removing Sandler (2006). These additions refine multilingual-pretraining and linguistic positioning; most of the existing related-work survey remains.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify glosses, VSSigns, dataset selection, and grouping results. V2 adds a Data Collection subsection and organized appendices, relocates dataset characteristics and limitations, and changes the affiliation from SaluteDevices to SberAI. The central narrative and most method exposition are retained.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reformats the document with narrower columns, larger typography, and reflowed tables and figures. The unchanged distribution figure moves to Appendix A as Figure 3; the pipeline becomes Figure 2 with updated Turkish-language labels. Tables gain rows, revised headers and footnotes, and Algorithm 1 adds a substantial new display.

improvement.justification: The MM-WLAuslan comparisons strengthen evidence for Logos against another large source corpus, while Appendices A–B make collection and training substantially easier to assess and reproduce. Table 3 also becomes consistent with the other frozen-encoder results. These are useful but bounded gains to an otherwise stable study; removing the explicit racial-bias qualification slightly reduces the specificity of its limitations.
